item.title: マスク氏とアンソロピック、ＡＩの富還元で異なる構想
item.description:
Abu Sultan
[１９日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）「クロード」を手がけるアンソロピックと実業家イーロン・...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
マスク氏とアンソロピック、ＡＩの富還元で異なる構想 10/19 11:12 配信

写真はアンソロピックのロゴ。6月5日に撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Abu Sultan

[１９日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）「クロード」を手がけるアンソロピックと実業家イーロン・マスク氏が、ＡＩブームで得られる富の一部を社会に還元する方法について、対照的な構想を示した。両者の違いは、ＡＩが生む巨額の利益が一般の人々に届く仕組みに影響を与える可能性がある。

アンソロピックは１８日、自社株の５％を新たな公益基金に拠出すると発表した。一方、マスク氏は１９日、「米国の全ての子ども」にスペースＸ株を１株ずつ贈ると約束。急成長するＡＩ業界に世間の厳しい目が向けられる中、こうした直接分配を支持した。

アンソロピックが非営利団体への寄付や特定の人々への直接給付を通じた富の分配を目指す一方、純資産が１兆ドル近くに上る世界一の富豪マスク氏は「株式を直接一般の人々に配る」ことを勧めると述べている。

アンソロピックの競合スペースＸＳＩを率いるマスク氏は１９日早朝の投稿で、「来年、私が保有するスペースＸ株を米国の全ての子どもに１株ずつ贈る。これは今後何度も行う取り組みの第一弾になる」と表明した。同氏は６月時点で同社株を約６４億２０００万株保有していた。

スペースＸの株価は１９日、約１％高で取引を終えた。

アンソロピックは、今回の取り組みによって、人類の利益のための寄付をより柔軟に、大規模に行えるようになると説明した。同社は現在、公益企業（ＰＢＣ）として史上最大規模の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を計画している。ＰＢＣは、より広範な公共の利益と収益目標の両立を経営陣に義務付ける法人形態だ。

ＩＰＯ時の企業価値は約２兆ドルとなる可能性がある。ただ、ロイターは先週、一部の投資家が約１兆５０００億ドルという、より低い評価額を検討していると独自に報じた。企業価値を１兆５０００億─２兆ドルとすると、基金に拠出する５％の株式の価値は７５０億─１０００億ドルとなる。

これは、マスク氏による株式贈与の想定額を大きく上回る。同氏の贈与額も相当な規模で、米国の子どもが７２００万人いるという国勢調査の数字に基づくと、現在の株価で約１１０億ドルとなる。

マスク氏は「将来の経済の持ち分である株式を人々に直接渡すのが正しい方法だ」と述べた。

ホワイトハウスは数カ月前、誕生から成人までの資産形成を支援する投資制度「トランプ口座」を開始した。２０２５─２８年に生まれた米国市民に政府が１０００ドルを拠出する投資口座を提供し、家族が資金を積み増せる仕組みだ。

トランプ米大統領は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、「トランプ口座を通じて数百万人の米国の子どもたちにスペースＸ株を贈るという、われわれの伝説的な友人イーロン・マスク氏の驚くほど寛大な行為に心から感謝する！」と表明した。

マスク氏によるスペースＸ株の寄付がトランプ口座と連動するのか、何らかの売却制限期間が設けられるのかについて、スペースＸから直ちに回答は得られなかった。

＜労働市場への影響に対応＞

アンソロピックは自社について、安全性を最優先するＡＩ開発企業と位置付けており、ＡＩには「人類に壊滅的な被害や存続の危機をもたらすリスク」があると指摘している。

同社はブログへの投稿で、公益基金の支援対象として、非営利団体への寄付、特定の人々への直接給付、ＡＩが労働市場に及ぼす影響への対応などを挙げた。同社は既に、労働市場の混乱の研究と対応に２億ドルを拠出すると表明しており、基金はこの取り組みを発展させるものとなる。

基金は完全所有の有限責任会社として設立する計画。アンソロピックの企業価値が未公表の基準額から５０％上昇するごとに、取締役会の裁量で同社株の２％が追加で拠出される。

同社は、基金が保有する株式を米国内外のロビー活動や政治献金に使うことはないと説明した。

共同創業者らが保有株式の８０％を寄付するとの約束や、従業員の寄付に会社が上乗せする制度を合わせると、将来追加される株式を除き、アンソロピック株の約２０％が公益目的に充てられることになる。

アンソロピックは、基金のガバナンスや組織構造、保有比率の拡大につながる企業価値の基準について、近く詳細を公表するとした。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず 最終更新: 10/20(火) 8:26 ロイター

item.title: インドネシア証取、自動注文拒否の下落率基準を7％に 年内適用
item.description: [ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - インドネシア証券取引所は１９日、自動で注文が拒否されるシステム「auto-rej...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インドネシア証取、自動注文拒否の下落率基準を7％に　年内適用 10/19 10:34 配信

写真はインドネシア証券取引所。　10月16日、ジャカルタで撮影。REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana

[ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - インドネシア証券取引所は１９日、自動で注文が拒否されるシステム「auto-rejection」の下落率基準を１５％から７％に変更したと発表した。

• この措置は同日発効し、今年１２月３１日まで適用される。

• 世界的な株価指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩは１６日、インドネシアの株式市場はもはや「エマージング（新興国）市場」ステータスに値していないとし、「スタンドアローン」ステータスへの移行プロセスに組み入れた。

• 同日のインドネシア主要株価指数は１１．５７％安で取引を終えた。１日当たりの下落率としては２８年ぶりの大きさ。

• 同取引所は声明で「今回の調整は投資家に利用可能な情報を評価・消化する機会を提供し、インドネシアの経済ファンダメンタルズ（基礎的条件）に基づいてより適切な投資判断を下せるよう支援することを目的としている」と説明。

• 今回の措置は、金融規制当局と、アナリストやエコノミストを含む資本市場関係者との間で週末に行われた会合を受けたもの。

• 同取引所はこのポリシーについて、市場の状況に応じて定期的に見直すと表明。

• この措置は、株価の下落率が７％に達した場合、特定の銘柄の取引を停止するための手段となる。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：北朝鮮が韓国と対立姿勢、米国にとって新たな悩みの種に 焦点：新興国投資ラッシュに取り残されるインドネシア、強い政策への不信感 アングル：スマトラ島豪雨被害、森林破壊で被害拡大か　地元に怒りの声 アングル：石炭依存の東南アジア、長期電力購入契約がエネ移行の妨げに 最終更新: 10/19(月) 10:34 ロイター

item.title: 金利への機動対応、上昇スピードや市場機能など総合判断＝日銀総裁
item.description:
Takahiko Wada Rie Ishiguro
［東京 １９日 ロイター］ - 日銀の植田和男総裁は１９日の参議...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
金利への機動対応、上昇スピードや市場機能など総合判断＝日銀総裁 10/19 10:13 配信

日銀の植田和男総裁。9月18日、東京で撮影。 REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Takahiko Wada　Rie Ishiguro

［東京　１９日　ロイター］ - 日銀の植田和男総裁は１９日の参議院予算委員会で、長期金利の推移に関連し、機動的なオペを行う「例外的な状況」について「前もって具体的にその内容を申し上げることは適切でない」と述べた。その上で、一般論としつつ「例えば金利が非常に速いスピードで上昇している、市場機能に深刻な問題が急に発生しているといった事情の有無等を踏まえ、その時々において総合的に判断していくことになる」と説明した。

浜野喜史委員（民主）の質問に答えた。物価動向については「基調的な物価上昇率が徐々に高まってきており、足元では２％にかなり近づいている」と評価した上で「２％程度の水準に安定させていく観点がより重要な局面になっている」との見解を改めて示した。

植田総裁は、短期金利が適切なペースで調整されず、物価上振れに対する先行き懸念や不確実性が高まると市場が認識した場合には、長期金利が上昇する可能性があるとし、「物価目標実現の観点から適切に金融政策運営していくことが、結果的に国債市場における安定的な金利形成にも資する」と話した。

足元のインフレが輸入物価の上昇を起点とするコストプッシュ型か、日銀が求めている賃金上昇を起点とするディマンドプル型かとの質問には「一般論としては明確に区別するのはなかなか難しい」と回答。中東情勢の影響によるエネルギーや原材料価格の上昇がさまざまな価格に波及していることは「ある種、コストプッシュ型インフレとみることができる」一方、グローバルな人工知能（ＡＩ）関連需要の好調が国内の設備投資や輸出を押し上げ、さまざまな価格上昇につながっている状況はディマンドプル型だと説明した。

その上で、景気が緩やかに回復し、労働需給が逼迫する中で、賃金上昇をさまざまな財やサービスの販売価格に転嫁する動きも続いていると総括した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：サービス価格上昇に加速の気配、日銀の緩和修正判断に影響も コラム：漸進的な日銀の緩和修正、ドル130円割れは短期間か＝植野大作氏 コラム：食品値下げは広がるのか、日銀判断にも影響する分岐点に コラム：日銀の背中押す春闘、植田総裁会見で占う「次」の展開 コラム：日銀マイナス金利解除、3月のイメージ強めた高田委員の発言 最終更新: 10/19(月) 12:51 ロイター

item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine got no warning as Russian missiles rain in
item.description: Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding that some vital deliveries from the United States were being delayed.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding that some vital deliveries from the United States were being delayed. Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Ten people were reported killed. A Russian drone attack killed six people, including two children, in a park near Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, according to the regional governor, Oleh Syniehubov. Zelenskiy called the strike "an act of absolute barbarity". In all, Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles overnight at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones in attacks stretching from Kharkiv and Dnipro in the east to Odesa in the south and Volyn and Rivne in the west. Two people were killed in Kyiv and the nearby region and two more in the industrial city of Kryvyi Rih, officials said. HIGH TENSIONS Tensions are running high between Zelenskiy and President Donald Trump's administration over US support for Ukraine and Washington's approach to Russia. "Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app. "When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defence are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners." Zelenskiy later said he had [USN:L4N4651DO TEXT:"discussed"] speeding up supplies of the Patriot system, vital to countering Russian ballistic missiles, with representatives of the US company Lockheed Martin. "It is their Patriot systems and F-16 planes that play an important role in defending against Russian ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones. The company is now boosting production of ballistic interceptors. We are hoping that we will be able to buy some of them to protect more lives," Zelenskiy said on Telegram. "And things are not easy on both fronts right now. We talked about how we can expand and increase supplies." For several months, Ukraine has suffered from critical shortages of US-made Patriot missiles. Zelenskiy said earlier that the United States had slowed some vital supplies for Ukraine, adding that the delays were at the US Defense Department level. He provided no other details. Kyiv has previously said it has struggled to get interceptors critical to repelling Russian missile attacks. Zelenskiy said that some political agreements on air defence were not implemented at a working level. Throughout the nearly five-year war, Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to detect Russian ballistic missile launches and provide early warning of incoming strikes. Yurii Ihnat, a spokesman for the Ukrainian air force, said Kyiv received no warning ahead of the first ballistic missile strike overnight but did receive information ahead of a second attack. "For some reason, no information was received the first time, a matter our experts are investigating together with our partners, as this is not the first time such a situation has occurred," Ihnat told Ukrainian television. Secretary of State Marco Rubio [USN:L1N465065 TEXT:"denied"] that the United States had paused some intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Ukrainian air defences downed 247 targets - four cruise missiles and 243 drones, the air force said. Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a "massive strike" using precision weapons and attack drones against Ukrainian defence industry facilities, drone and cruise missile storage sites, and a data centre. Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said the energy sector was the main target of the attacks, with damage reported across the country. Ukraine's energy ministry said rolling blackouts were introduced for households and businesses as crews worked to restore supplies. Koretskyi said Russia has hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure more than 2,000 times since mid-July, intensifying its attacks from previous years of the war.

item.title: US stocks rebound with AI earnings test ahead, euro falls on France unrest
item.description: The Nasdaq rose more than 1% on Monday as tech shares rebounded ahead of a big week for AI-related earnings, while European stocks and the euro fell as unrest in France added to concerns about the country's fiscal outlook.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch, Danilo Masoni
item.content:encoded: The Nasdaq rose more than 1% on Monday as tech shares rebounded ahead of a big week for AI-related earnings, while European stocks and the euro fell as unrest in France added to concerns about the country's fiscal outlook. [USN:L6N4650X5 TEXT:"French bonds and Paris-listed stocks"] also fell as the widespread protests across France underscored the difficulties the government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's central government asked some local authorities to impose curfews as it faced pressure over security failings on Monday, after looting stemming from the protests. Tech stocks on Wall Street recovered some ground after a bruising week, with an index of semiconductors (.SOX) up 1.6%. On Friday, the index sank in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008. With results due from Meta (META.O) on Wednesday, and results from Tesla (TSLA.O) and chipmakers Lam Research (LRCX.O) and Texas Instruments (TXN.O) also due this week, investors will be watching for signs that massive AI spending ultimately pays off. "Investors are buying the correction dip that we had," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York. "The market is now going to go through a very critical test over the next two weeks. We have some big-name earnings coming out," he said. "In terms of technology, the test of whether or not the spending on AI... will be met with satisfaction is going to be critical." The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 36.38 points, or 0.07%, to 51,966.03, the S&P 500 (.SPX) rose 31.29 points, or 0.41%, to 7,690.73 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) rose 290.85 points, or 1.11%, to 26,430.89. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) rose 0.88 points, or 0.08%, to 1,129.98. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers expected to increase combined capital expenditure to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Results from SpaceX (SPCX.O) are also due on Tuesday. Overall, US earnings are still expected to rise about 30%, largely driven by growth in the technology sector. [USN:L6N46514T TEXT:"US Treasury yields"] rose on Monday, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield coming off its biggest weekly drop in seven months, as concerns about the impact of higher interest rates on AI stocks abated. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was up 4.2 basis points at 5.14%. The recent bond selloff had also intensified scrutiny of the AI sector's massive funding needs. In economic data, the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market index on Monday showed a drop of three points to 29 this month, the lowest level since June 2012 and below the 31 estimate of economists polled by Reuters. Recent comments from Federal Reserve officials, including Chair Kevin Warsh, suggest policymakers are in no rush to hike rates again. On Friday, Warsh expressed optimism about US economic strength but gave no indication of whether or when more hikes will be needed. EUROPEAN STOCKS, EURO FALL The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index fell 0.8%, while France's blue-chip CAC 40 index (.FCHI) dropped 1.1%. France's 10-year yield earlier was up 13 basis points to 4.9% while the German 10-year yield, the benchmark for the euro zone, was also higher. The spread between French OATs and safe-haven German Bunds has widened to 147 basis points, trading at levels last seen during the 2011 to 2012 European debt crisis, from around 110 bps in late September. [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"Widespread weekend unrest"] in the euro zone's second-largest economy underscored the challenge facing the French government as it seeks to reduce its large budget deficit ahead of next year's presidential elections. The euro fell 0.24% to $1.1212. The US dollar was boosted by the rebound in tech stocks. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.17% to 101.97. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar rose 0.49% versus the greenback after data showed China's economic growth rebounded from three-year lows, expanding at a 4.5% annual pace in the third quarter. Oil prices were mixed, with investors digesting attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on a Yemeni military training camp and renewed attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military facilities. Brent crude futures fell 31 cents to settle at $109.55 a barrel. Brent fell more than $3 earlier in the session. US West Texas Intermediate gained $2.25 to $103.66 a barrel, the highest settlement since September 15. Spot gold fell 0.61% to $4,139.67 an ounce.

item.title: Antofagasta’s Centinela strike ends after deal with unions
item.description: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contra
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contract, ending a strike of more than a week, the unions and the company said on Sunday. More than 700 members of the Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions began the strike on October 7 after contract talks broke down. They had sought equal benefits for workers regardless of which union they belonged to. The parties returned to the negotiating table on Tuesday in an effort to resolve the dispute. “The Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions announce the successful conclusion of our collective bargaining process, after 94.49% of participating workers voted to approve the proposed collective agreement,” the unions said in a statement, which was followed by a company statement confirming the deal. Three workers had been on a hunger strike in an effort to pressure both sides into finding a solution to the deadlocked talks. Antofagasta said on Wednesday it had managed to maintain production at normal levels, avoiding any negative impact from the strike at the mine, which produced 240,400 metric tons of copper in 2025. The strike at Centinela, along with the ultimately unrealized risk of a supervisors’ strike at BHP’s Escondida mine, had been supporting global copper prices amid concerns about the industry’s ability to increase supply sufficiently to meet expected future demand. (Reporting by Fabian Cambero; Editing by William Mallard)

item.description: UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.

US officials visit Palestinian village after settler attacks on diplomats

UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.

US Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labor Riley Barnes visits the Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh near Ramallah, a day after Israeli militant settlers attacked a French mayor and European diplomats during olive harvest, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 18, 2026. FAST

TAYBEH, West Bank: US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday (Oct 18) following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on European diplomats and an American photojournalist in the previous two days. Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labor, Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet with members of the Christian community in Taybeh. Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Saturday by masked Israeli settlers. The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village.

The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump endorsing his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel's parliamentary election on Oct 27. Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian and longtime supporter of Israel, earlier wrote on X calling for "those who attacked" the Washington Post photojournalist, a US citizen, to be jailed.

Related:

Israel denounces 'grotesque absurdity' of Macron UN remarks on West Bank

Israel's Netanyahu orders West Bank settler outposts to be removed, sources say

US ambassador visits Palestinian town amid rise in West Bank settler violence

NETANYAHU CIRCUMSPECT ON SETTLER VIOLENCE Trump has expressed his opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank, but his administration has put little pressure on Netanyahu's right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military both blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect. He has said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" with the Israeli military, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are "unclear". France urged Israeli authorities to arrest Saturday's attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Sunday there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents.

Israeli settlers attack a journalist in Abu Falah, West Bank Oct 16, 2026, in this screengrab from a video. (Photo: Andrey X/via REUTERS)

The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinian s. Settler attacks on the Palestinian s are surging, with at least 170 since Sep 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare. On Sunday, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinian s and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee. Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Musk, Anthropic outline dueling approaches to AI-era philanthropy
item.description: Anthropic and Elon Musk have laid out sharply different blueprints for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom, a split that may shape how the technology's financial windfall reaches the public.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Sophia, Abu Sultan
item.content:encoded: Anthropic and Elon Musk have laid out sharply different blueprints for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom, a split that may shape how the technology's financial windfall reaches the public. The creator of Claude models said over the weekend it is committing 5% of its shares to an unprecedented new fund for the "public good," while Musk pledged on Monday to give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America", arguing for such direct distributions as the burgeoning sector faces public scrutiny. Security breaches involving AI systems and warnings from industry leaders that runaway development of the technology could pose severe, even existential, risks have deepened AI safety concerns, adding to public anxiety over job losses. While Anthropic is betting on distributing wealth through nonprofit donations and direct contributions to specific populations, Musk, the world's richest person with a net worth of nearly $1 trillion, has said he recommends "giving the shares directly to the public". "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk, who runs Anthropic rival SpaceXSI, said in a post early on Monday. He held about 6.42 billion shares in the company as of June. SpaceX (SPCX.O) shares closed up about 1% on Monday. Anthropic said its initiative will give it more flexibility and scale to make donations for the benefit of humanity. The company is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a [USN:L6N45L0UH TEXT:"public benefit corporation"], a legal structure that requires management to balance broader public interests with profitability goals. The flotation could value it at roughly $2 trillion, although Reuters exclusively [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"reported"] last week that some investors are weighing a lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion. That would value a 5% stake toward the fund in a range of $75 billion to $100 billion. It would dwarf the still substantial potential value of Musk's share giveaway, which would be worth roughly $11 billion at current share prices based on US census figures showing there are 72 million children in America. "Giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way," Musk said. Musk's move comes months after the White House launched "Trump Accounts," a cradle-to-adulthood investment program that will provide US citizens born between 2025 and 2028 a government-funded investment account of $1,000 that families can build on. With the option for individuals and corporations to donate equity shares to the accounts, many top US companies including Dell (DELL.N) , Visa (V.N) , Micron (MU.O) and Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) have already pledged support for the program with employer matches or additional funding. "A BIG THANK YOU to our legendary friend, Elon Musk, for his incredible generosity in giving SpaceX Stock to millions of American children through TRUMP ACCOUNTS!," President Donald Trump said in a post on social media platform Truth Social. SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request on whether Musk's SpaceX share donations would be linked to Trump Accounts or come with any kind of lockup period. Earlier this year, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under the Trump initiative. "That's a lot of shares... I'm sure somebody will be happy to take them," Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth Management, who does not hold SpaceX shares in the portfolios he manages, said of Musk's announcement. "It feels like a publicity stunt... Will it create positive public sentiment? Perhaps." Michael Dell and his wife Susan have pledged $6.25 billion in cash for Trump Accounts, aimed specifically at underprivileged children. In contrast, the value of Musk's contribution will depend on SpaceX's often volatile share performance. Most of Musk's philanthropic efforts have been through the Musk Foundation, which reportedly holds more than $14 billion in assets. Berkshire Hathaway (BRKa.N) Chairman Emeritus Warren Buffett, one of the most prominent figures in philanthropy, is reported to have given away $60 billion so far, with most of the rest of his roughly $150 billion fortune slated for philanthropy too. The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has distributed more than $100 billion since its founding in 2000, with some of that fueled by donations from Buffett. LABOR MARKET IMPACT CITED Anthropic, which has positioned itself as a safety-first AI lab, has said AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity." The company said in its blog post its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI's impact on the labor market, building on a previously announced $200 million commitment to study and address labor market disruption. Its proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. Global companies have [USN:L6N42P0Q1 TEXT:"cut"] thousands of jobs after investing heavily in AI, with many, primarily tech firms, pointing to higher efficiencies from the technology's rapid adoption. NOT FOR POLITICAL GIVING The AI giant said none of the equity held by its fund would be used for lobbying or political giving in the US or abroad. US [USN:L6N43N198 TEXT:"policymakers"] are weighing greater oversight of AI and companies are stepping up efforts to shape how the technology is regulated. Combined with its co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity and an employee donation matching program, roughly 20% of Anthropic's shares will be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares added later. Anthropic said it would say more soon on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake.

item.title: Strong winds fuelled grass fire at Canadian military base that killed four
item.description: The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210km east of Edmonton in Alberta.
item.dc:creator: CNA

Strong winds fuelled grass fire at Canadian military base that killed four

The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210km east of Edmonton in Alberta.

A sign for Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire that caused deaths and injuries, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada on Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Jennifer Gauthier)

FAST

CALGARY: Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smouldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday (Oct 18). Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which Prime Minister Mark Carney described as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil. Winds up to 96km per hour fed the blaze which began around 4pm MDT on Saturday. But they were below 50kmh leading up to the fire, Major General Wade Rutland told reporters at a news conference. He described the sudden high winds and resulting spread of the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event in which the flames advanced 1km in 30 to 60 seconds.

"I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210km west of the military site. Officials identified the dead as Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark. "The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honour the victims. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said many of the injured will require "weeks and months" of specialised, intensive medical care. When the fire began, Rutland said, 85 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, were in "high intensity" combat training using live munitions at the base, which is located in a prairie setting. The soldiers were preparing for deployment to Latvia, where Canadian forces currently have their largest international military operation. Rutland said the incident remains under investigation and declined to speculate on what caused the grass fire. Officials do not believe the region's extensive oil and gas infrastructure had anything to do with the incident, he said. He also ruled out "outside interference." CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country.

People attend a church service, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire caused deaths and injuries at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada, Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jennifer Gauthier)

Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable", Carney said. Twenty-two ground ambulances and eight air ambulances responded to the scene, Smith said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer. Military search and rescue technicians also parachuted into the site, Rutland said. Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright. The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

Source: Reuters/fs/ec

Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli election

The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

US President Donald Trump points his finger towards Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as they shake hands during a press conference after meeting at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, Dec 29, 2025. (Photo: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst)

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 18) endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minster" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilising regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure - But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel." The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the Oct 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

Related:

Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections

Israel top court puts Arab parties back on ballot

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to Trump on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries, including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

Source: Reuters/fs
